candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — bed-rail risk and safety-device reassessment
candidate.educational_objective: Reassess bed-rail use in confused older adults because rails may create entrapment or climbing-related fall hazards rather than reliably preventing injury.

options.A: Keep full-length rails raised and increase rounding because rails remain appropriate fall-prevention barriers even when the client is climbing over them.
options.B: Pad the rail openings and continue full-length rails without reassessment because padding alone removes the main entrapment and climbing risks.
options.C: Use all full-length rails whenever confusion worsens because additional rails reduce unsupervised bed exit without creating meaningful additional hazards.
options.D: Full-length rails can create entrapment and climbing-related fall hazards, so the nurse should reassess whether the rails increase rather than reduce this client's risk.

candidate.rationale: FDA bed-safety guidance identifies frail, elderly and confused patients as vulnerable to bed-rail entrapment and notes that climbing over rails can result in more serious falls. FDA recommends individual patient assessment rather than routine bed-rail use. D therefore identifies the relevant safety concern. A and C assume rails are protective despite observed climbing, and B incorrectly assumes padding eliminates the need for reassessment.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Older/confused patients are at increased entrapment risk; bed rails can lead to more serious injuries when patients climb over them; bed-rail use should be based on individualized assessment rather than routine use.
